### AI review findings ledger

Written by the AI Review workflow, one entry per round, so the finding set is cumulative across rounds rather than evaporating with each runner (#1168).

A `findings` of null means the round was NOT measured — the payload was absent or unparseable. An empty array means the round was read and found nothing. They are different facts.

THIS IS A WINDOW, NOT A HISTORY. At most 12 rounds are retained, and fewer when they would not fit — a comment body has a hard 65536 character limit, so the body is rendered and measured before it is written. `truncated` is how many rounds have fallen off the front of it, by either route. A dropped round is gone rather than empty, so a finding only that round recorded can no longer be carried forward; without the count, nothing downstream could tell that from a finding nobody ever raised. An ABSENT `truncated` means the depth is unknown, which is not the same as zero.

`identity` names the rule the per-finding anchors were recorded under. A reader that does not recognise it carries those findings without keying them, rather than keying them under a rule they were not recorded with. `text` is the content of the cited line at the time, which is the anchor that rule uses; a finding with no `text` cannot be shown resolved and is carried.

Each round records the `verdict` word the reviewer wrote beside its findings, transcribed and not validated, and each finding records its `failure_scenario` (#1511). Those two with `findings` are the whole of what the adjudicator reads, so a round entry can be replayed through it rather than re-decided. A `verdict` of null means no word was readable; no `verdict` key at all means the round was written before this was recorded. Nothing here is ever shortened to fit: a round is dropped whole, because a cut field reads as a complete one.
